reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA2 publishes 14 MW of IT capacity, ranking 17th among Virginia facilities with disclosed power figures and contributing roughly 1 percent of the state's 1,326 published MW.

At this scale, 14 MW supports approximately 350 racks at 40 kW per rack, a density typical of AI training workloads, or roughly 1,400 racks at 10 kW per rack for mixed colocation use. The operator has not published redundancy tier, power usage effectiveness, floor area, or network connectivity details, so the actual workload density cannot be confirmed from available sources. The facility sits in Ashburn, Virginia's densest colocation market, but remains mid-to-small by the standards of that corridor, where major campuses routinely exceed 100 MW. Nothing in the published record indicates optimization for high-density AI loads, though nothing excludes it. A meaningful assessment of suitability for AI training would require rack-level power density and cooling specifications that NTT has not disclosed on its facility page.
